description.narrative: The "Sharakat II" project has meticulously designed a suite of activities aimed at addressing thecritical challenges faced by young men and women in Yemen, particularly their exclusion fromdecision-making and leadership roles in a conflict-ridden environment. These activities arestrategically aligned to foster inclusion, build capacity, and enhance the representation of youthand women in peacebuilding and governance.To tackle the inadequate capacity and empowerment of young men and women, Sharakat IIplans to implement a series of training programs and workshops. These are intended to equipthem with essential skills in leadership, governance, advocacy, and civic engagement. Byenhancing their capabilities, the project aims to prepare them for active and effectiveparticipation in decision-making processes at various levels.Recognizing the need for more robust platforms where young people can interact with decision-makers, the project proposes the establishment of regular forums and dialogue platforms. These will facilitate direct interactions between young men and women and local authorities, political parties, and other stakeholders. Such platforms are not only meant to voice youth concerns and ideas but also to integrate their perspectives into ongoing peace and governance dialogues, thereby addressing their historical exclusion.Sharakat II will focus on four governorates: Aden, Taiz, Hadramout and Marib. These selections aim to achieve a socio-political balance by including both northern (Taiz and Marib) and southern (Aden and Hadramout) regions, considering their demographic significance.Sharakat II will maintain its focus on the governorates of Aden, Taiz, and Hadramout, expanding upon the groundwork established in Sharakat I. These governorates are strategic for several reasons. Firstly, these governorates have been identified based on their significance in the context of peacebuilding efforts in Yemen and their existing involvement in the Sharakat project during its initial phase. Secondly, focusing on these governorates allows for buildingupon the achievements and investments made in CSOs and youth groups during Sharakat I, ensuring continuity and sustainability of efforts. Additionally, these governorates present opportunities to further promote youth political participation by engaging with prominentpolitical parties operating in these governorates beyond what has been achieved in Phase I.The main project partners are the Civil Alliance of Peace (CAP) and the Youth Peace and Security Pact (YPS- PACT).
